name: Brazil
governanceModel: Comprehensive risk-based AI bill pending final passage
debateTopics: Whether PL 2338 passes before the August 2026 recess
overview:
Brazil's comprehensive AI bill, PL 2338/2023, has been working through Congress since May 2023. The Senate approved a substitute text in December 2024, and as of May 2026 it remains pending in the Chamber of Deputies, with amendments expected — biometric surveillance carve-outs are a particular sticking point. It's expected to reach a vote before the August 2026 recess, though enforcement provisions likely won't take effect before late 2026 even if passed.

The bill centres enforcement on ANPD, Brazil's data protection authority, using a risk-based framework similar in spirit to the EU AI Act. Alongside the legislation, the government's Brazilian AI Plan (PBIA) runs across five axes — infrastructure, training and capacity, public-service improvement, business innovation, and regulation and governance support — and the IA² programme has supported 127 AI startups since 2022.

debates.summary: Negotiations over how PL 2338 treats biometric surveillance are a key sticking point holding up the bill's final passage.
debates.expanded: Law enforcement and security agencies have pushed for carve-outs allowing continued use of biometric surveillance technologies that the bill's general risk-based framework might otherwise restrict. Civil-liberties groups oppose broad exemptions, arguing they would undermine the bill's core protections just for the use case most associated with rights concerns.

debates.topic: Whether PL 2338 passes before the August 2026 recess
debates.summary: After years of progress, PL 2338's final passage now comes down to whether the Chamber of Deputies can reach a vote before its August 2026 recess.
debates.expanded: The bill has already survived a multi-year process including Senate approval of a substitute text in December 2024. Missing the August 2026 recess deadline wouldn't kill the bill outright, but would extend Brazil's current status as one of the few major economies still without comprehensive binding AI legislation.
